You are reading a local Kanban board to help produce a phased build plan for "Kodely", an AI website builder.

Fetch the board:
  curl -s "http://localhost:3001/api/board?boardId=720aa8c1-d259-4e49-b777-c58965efabd1"

It returns JSON: {columns:[{id,name,position}], cards:[{id,columnId,title,description,...}]}.

Read EVERY card (title AND full description) in these columns ONLY:
  - "Tech & Architecture"
  - "AI / Codegen Engine"

Write a node script to filter and print them; do not try to read the whole board by eye.

Return a digest with:
1. For each card: a one-line essence in your own words.
2. Classify each as: FOUNDATIONAL (other things depend on it), SCALING (only needed at volume), or OPTIMISATION (cost/quality improvement).
3. Note DEPENDENCIES precisely — especially anything requiring: a server-side sandbox (Firecracker/microVM), per-project database isolation, a build worker/queue, or hosting infrastructure.
4. Estimate each as S (<1 day), M (2-5 days), L (1-3 weeks), XL (>1 month).
5. Flag cards already satisfied by what exists today: server-side `vite build` against one pre-installed locked dependency tree (never npm install per generation), a self-repair loop that retries a failed build once with the error fed back, checkpoint snapshots of the full file tree, publish-time secret scanning, coarse per-user rate limits, a model router with configurable model+effort per build phase, and prompt caching on the system prompt.

Be concise per card. Accuracy about dependencies and sequencing matters most. Return the digest as your final message; it is data for me, not a human-facing report.

4	########## COLUMN: Tech & Architecture (42 cards) ##########
5	
6	=== [1] Evaluate WebContainers licensing + Safari/SharedArrayBuffer limits ===
7	WebContainers boot Node in-browser in milliseconds and even re-run `npm install` on every load for a clean env, but they depend on `SharedArrayBuffer`, which requires COOP/COEP cross-origin-isolation headers and **does not work in Safari** ([sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/docs/advanced-usage/nodebox), [blog.stackblitz.com](https://blog.stackblitz.com/posts/introducing-webcontainers/)). WebContainers are also a commercial StackBlitz product with per-seat/enterprise licensing, not a free dependency. Kodely should treat WebContainers as an *optional fast-preview add-on* for pure-frontend projects, not the core, and confirm license cost before committing. Document the browser-support matrix so support doesn't get blindsided by Safari users seeing a blank preview.
8	
9	=== [2] Consider Sandpack/Nodebox for lightweight frontend previews ===
10	CodeSandbox's **Sandpack** is an open-source (MIT) in-browser bundler with hot-module-reload and error overlays, and **Nodebox** runs Node in *any* browser (including Safari) because it avoids SharedArrayBuffer, with out-of-the-box support for Next.js, Vite and Astro ([codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2](https://codesandbox.io/blog/announcing-sandpack-2), [sandpack.codesandbox.io](https://sandpack.codesandbox.io/)). The tradeoff: Nodebox targets small projects/examples and can't reach full Node API compatibility. For Kodely's early free tier, Sandpack could power an instant, zero-infra-cost preview of generated React components before a project graduates to a real sandbox. Cheap way to make the first-render feel instant.
11	
12	=== [3] Pick a cloud-sandbox provider: E2B vs Daytona vs Modal vs Fly ===
13	If not using Nxeon's own VMs, the market leaders differ sharply. **E2B** uses Firecracker microVMs (hardware-level isolation, ~150ms cold start, ephemeral) and reports 88% of Fortune 100 signed up; **Daytona** uses shared-kernel containers with faster ~90ms cold starts and *persistent* stateful workspaces better suited to long-running iterative agents; **Modal** and **Fly Machines** offer their own Firecracker-based compute ([northflank.com/blog/daytona-vs-e2b-ai-code-execution-sandboxes](https://northflank.com/blog/daytona-vs-e2b-ai-code-execution-sandboxes), [blog.logrocket.com](https://blog.logrocket.com/comparing-ai-agent-sandbox-platforms-e2b-modal-daytona-and-more/)). Note Daytona moved production closed-source in June 2026. Pricing is ~$0.05/vCPU-hr + ~$0.016/GiB-hr billed per second on both. Kodely should benchmark E2B (isolation) vs Daytona (persistence) against a self-hosted option before locking in.
14	
15	=== [4] Self-host sandboxes on Nxeon Proxmox using Firecracker microVMs ===
16	E2B's isolation model is literally Firecracker microVMs — the same tech behind AWS Lambda — giving per-sandbox kernel isolation ([spheron.network/blog/ai-agent-code-execution-sandbox-e2b-daytona-firecracker](https://www.spheron.network/blog/ai-agent-code-execution-sandbox-e2b-daytona-firecracker/)). Nxeon already runs Proxmox VMs, so Kodely can run its own Firecracker (or lightweight VM/container) sandbox fleet on the same hardware, avoiding per-second sandbox vendor fees and keeping customer code on infra Nxeon controls. This directly reuses the existing Proxmox topology (the live .200 / dev .215 split noted in memory) — provision a *separate* sandbox host pool so builder workloads never touch the Soul Pilates prod box. Big cost + control win versus renting E2B/Daytona.
17	
18	=== [5] Default generated stack: Vite + React + TS + Tailwind + shadcn/ui ===
19	This is the de-facto winning combo. Lovable generates a single-page React app scaffolded with **Vite + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui + React Router**, deliberately *not* Next.js App Router ([vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack](https://vibe-eval.com/guides/lovable-tech-stack/), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). shadcn/ui matters because it's copy-in component source (not a locked dependency), so the AI can freely edit it and output stays consistent and good-looking. Kodely should ship this as the default template for pure web-app builds — it's fast to preview, easy for the model to reason about, and produces attractive UI out of the box.
20	
21	=== [6] Offer a Next.js full-stack template (rocket.new / v0 style) ===
22	For apps that need server routes, SSR, and a real backend in one repo, rocket.new generates **production Next.js** apps and v0 generates full-stack Next.js with API routes and DB integration ([docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction](https://docs.rocket.new/getting-started/introduction), [blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://blog.tooljet.com/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). This is exactly Nxeon's existing stack (Next.js + Prisma + Postgres), so Kodely can reuse Nxeon's build/deploy tooling and conventions with almost no new work for this template. 228	Bolt instruments WebContainers at the **process, runtime, and build levels** so the agent receives 'the state of the application and the errors from Node.js or the browser console' and can auto-fix ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). This closed error loop is why its output actually runs. Kodely must capture build output, dev-server logs, uncaught runtime exceptions, and browser console errors from the sandbox and pipe them structured into the agent's next turn. Without this, the model is fixing blind. Build the error-capture channel as part of the sandbox from the start.
229	
230	=== [5] Context management for growing codebases — retrieve, don't dump ===
231	Bolt maximizes context ('the entire state of the application') for accuracy, but that only scales while projects are small ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Chroma's Context Rot study found *every* frontier model degrades as input grows — a 200K window can show serious accuracy loss by 50K tokens, and facts buried mid-context cost 30+ accuracy points ([cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely needs a retrieval layer: send the full tree/manifest but only the *relevant* file bodies (via embeddings + recent-edit heuristics), and keep the most important context at the start/end of the prompt. Plan retrieval before projects get big.
232	
233	=== [6] Prompt caching — the single biggest cost lever ===
234	Prompt caching gives a ~90% discount on cached input tokens and is the largest cost reducer for repeated system prompts; in Claude Code/Cline sessions, re-sending conversation history is ~50–60% of token spend and tool descriptions alone add 10–15K tokens per request ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should structure prompts so the stable system prompt, tool definitions, and unchanging project context sit in cacheable prefixes with Anthropic cache breakpoints. This is low-effort, high-savings and should be wired in before launch, not retrofitted.
235	
236	=== [7] Context compaction / conversation summarization ===
237	Long build sessions bloat context; Claude's context-compaction can condense history server-side (one reported case collapsed 132K tokens to 2K) and 'isolating work across separate context windows' keeps tasks from contaminating each other ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely should summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, and maintain a compact rolling project-state summary rather than replaying the whole chat each turn. Keeps long iterative sessions affordable and accurate.
238	
239	=== [8] Tool-use design: give the agent fs, terminal, npm, and console tools ===
240	Bolt gives the model complete control of the filesystem, node server, package manager, terminal and browser console ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should expose a tight, well-described tool set — write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server — each mapped to sandbox operations. Keep tool descriptions lean (they're billed on every call) and prefer a few composable tools over many niche ones. Good tool ergonomics are what let the model self-correct instead of guessing.
241	
242	=== [9] Retrieval/index over the project (file tree + embeddings) ===
243	When an agent lacks retrieval it wastes tokens reading whole files to find a few lines — the third-biggest token sink after history and tools ([fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization](https://fast.io/resources/ai-agent-token-cost-optimization/)). Vector DBs work but get expensive; a hybrid of efficient file storage + targeted embedding search often costs less ([pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage](https://pinggy.io/blog/tools_to_reduce_ai_coding_agent_token_usage/)). Kodely should maintain a live project index (symbol map + embeddings, refreshed on edits) so the agent can grep/semantic-search to the exact files it needs. Reuse Nxeon's existing Postgres with pgvector rather than adding a new vector DB.
244	
245	=== [10] System/prompt design + a structured artifact output format ===
246	Bolt's quality comes largely from a carefully engineered system prompt that constrains the model into its step-by-step flow and a structured 'artifact' format for emitting files/commands (public in the open-source repo) ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should define a strict output schema — plan block, then file-write and shell-command actions the runner parses deterministically — so parsing never depends on fragile prose. Invest real effort in the system prompt (stack conventions, when to diff vs rewrite, security rules); it's the cheapest quality lever and it's cacheable.
247	
248	=== [11] Stream generation to the UI (files + reasoning live) ===
249	Modern builders stream file writes and reasoning as they happen so users see progress instead of a spinner; this is core to the bolt/Lovable UX ([github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new](https://github.com/stackblitz/bolt.new)). Kodely should stream the model's tokens, surface each file being created/edited in real time, and show the plan up front. Streaming also lets users interrupt/redirect early, saving tokens on wrong directions. Reuse the streaming plumbing from Nxeon's existing Build-with-AI/chat agent.
250	
251	=== [12] Token metering + credit system (don't repeat Bolt's flat-rate mistake) ===
252	Bolt launched at $9/mo flat 'Netflix-model' access and users burned through allocations in weeks, creating scaling tension with inference cost ([latent.space/p/bolt](https://www.latent.space/p/bolt)). Kodely must meter token/compute usage per user from day one, expose a credits balance, and price plans against real Anthropic + sandbox cost. Track cost per project/message so heavy users are identifiable. Tie this to Nxeon's existing billing. This is a business-survival item, not an optimization.
253	
254	=== [13] Execution-based evals: pass@k + a regression harness ===
255	Real codegen quality is measured by *running* the output, not reading it — generate code, run it in a sandbox, check against tests, with pass@k as the headline metric; system-level evals also cover retrieval, prompt design, tool use and guardrails ([promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents](https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/guides/evaluate-coding-agents/), [futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). Kodely should build an eval suite of representative prompts ('todo app with auth', 'Stripe checkout page') that generates, boots the app in a sandbox, and asserts it builds + core flows work — run on every prompt/model change to catch regressions before shipping to users. Prevents silent quality drops when tweaking prompts or swapping models.
256	
257	=== [14] Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, and code-injection scanners ===
258	Coding agents are attack surfaces — a Feb 2026 attack on the Cline IDE started with a malicious GitHub issue *title* containing injected instructions; defenses need input guardrails (screen prompts) and output guardrails (screen generated code) ([futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026](https://futureagi.com/blog/evaluating-coding-agents-2026/)). A SecretsScanner catches invented/leaked credentials and a CodeInjectionScanner flags eval/exec/shell-interpolation/template-injection in generated code. Because Kodely will read user repos, GitHub issues, and pasted content into the agent, it must sanitize untrusted input and scan every generated file before commit/deploy. Given the CRITICAL RCE already found in Nxeon's DB Studio (memory), treat agent guardrails as a launch gate with a security review.
259	
260	=== [15] shadcn/ui component retrieval for consistent, attractive UI ===
261	A big reason Lovable/v0 output looks good is that they generate against **shadcn/ui**, whose components are editable source the model can retrieve and adapt rather than invent styling from scratch ([techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0](https://techsy.io/en/blog/lovable-vs-bolt-vs-v0/)). Kodely should ship a curated component/block library (shadcn + a few opinionated layout blocks) and give the agent a retrieval tool to pull the right component source into edits, so UI stays consistent and polished across a project. This also cuts tokens (the model composes known components instead of hand-writing markup). Bonus: encode Nxeon's own brand theme (navy+violet+cyan per memory) as a preset for on-brand builds.
262	
263	=== [16] Model routing + graceful degradation / fallback ===
264	Kodely will depend on Anthropic availability, and memory notes the Nxeon chat agent already ships a failure banner + graceful-degrade pattern for exactly this. Kodely should route by task (cheap model for trivial edits, Sonnet for codegen, Opus for planning), fall back to a secondary model/provider on outages or rate limits, and surface a clear degraded-mode banner instead of failing silently. Retry with backoff on transient errors and cap retries to protect token spend. Reuse the Nxeon chat agent's degradation UX directly.
265	
266	=== [17] Optional multi-agent decomposition (planner / coder / reviewer) ===
267	Research on LLM multi-agent code generation shows splitting roles (a planner, a coder, and a reviewer/tester) can improve reliability on complex builds by isolating concerns into separate context windows ([arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2604.16321), [cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026](https://cruxdigits.nl/blog/context-engineering-ai-agents-2026/)). Kodely could add a lightweight reviewer pass that runs the eval/build and critiques the coder's output before showing the user. Keep it optional/behind a flag — it multiplies token cost, so gate it to complex prompts or paid tiers. Start single-agent, add this only if evals show it moves quality.
268	
269	=== [18] Auto-SEO for generated sites ===
270	Every generated site ships with sensible meta tags, OpenGraph/Twitter images, a sitemap, and structured data. Users won't add these; making sites rank is a real value-add.
271	
272	=== [19] Accessibility + performance budget on output ===
273	Run a11y checks and a Lighthouse/perf budget on generated output, and auto-fix common failures. Quality bar that separates Kodely from slop-generators.
274	
275	=== [20] Prompt/guardrail library + eval harness ===
276	A versioned library of system prompts + guardrails and an execution-based eval harness so engine changes are regression-tested (green-build-first-try can't silently drop).
277	
278	=== [21] Large-project context management ===
279	Diff-based edits, file targeting, and retrieval so the engine stays reliable as projects grow beyond a single file/context window. The scaling wall most builders hit.
280

Read all 63 cards (42 in Tech & Architecture, 21 in AI / Codegen Engine) via a filter script. Digest below. `T#`/`A#` = card index within its column.

---

## TECH & ARCHITECTURE (42)

**T1 — WebContainers licensing / Safari limits** — Decide whether StackBlitz WebContainers are viable given SharedArrayBuffer + COOP/COEP + no-Safari + commercial licence; conclusion is "optional add-on, not core." • OPTIMISATION (research/decision) • Deps: none • **S** • Partly moot — you already build server-side, so this is a "don't do it" decision.

**T2 — Sandpack/Nodebox in-browser preview** — Free-tier zero-infra client-side preview of generated React before graduating to a real sandbox. • OPTIMISATION (COGS) • Deps: none (parallel path to server build) • **M** • Competes with existing server-side `vite build`; only worth it as a latency/cost play.

**T3 — Pick cloud sandbox vendor (E2B/Daytona/Modal/Fly)** — Buy-vs-buy comparison for server-side code execution; isolation (Firecracker) vs persistence (containers). • FOUNDATIONAL (decision gate) • Deps: **blocks/blocked-by T4** — mutually exclusive build-vs-buy • **S** (decision) / **M** with benchmarks.

**T4 — Self-host Firecracker microVMs on Proxmox** — Run own microVM sandbox fleet on Nxeon hardware to kill per-second vendor fees and keep code on owned infra. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: **is the sandbox dependency** — needed by T10, T15, T17, T18, T32, T33, T34, A4, A8; needs T39 (separate sandbox VM w/ nested KVM) • **XL**.

**T5 — Default stack Vite+React+TS+Tailwind+shadcn** — Ship the Lovable-style SPA template as the default generation target. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: none • **M** • **LIKELY ALREADY SATISFIED** — the locked pre-installed dependency tree implies this template already exists; card reduces to formalising it.

**T6 — Next.js full-stack template** — Second first-class template (SSR + API routes + Prisma/Postgres) matching Nxeon's own stack. • FOUNDATIONAL for full-stack tier • Deps: needs **per-project DB (T33)**, a real server runtime, and hosting (T11) — cannot ride the locked-dep `vite build` path • **L**.

**T7 — Backend choice: Supabase vs Convex vs Neon vs Nxeon Postgres** — Decide the default generated-app backend; recommends Nxeon-hosted Postgres+Prisma. • FOUNDATIONAL (decision) • Deps: gates T6, T8, T17, T33 • **S** decision / **L** to implement.

**T8 — Batteries-included auth scaffold per template** — Pre-wired login/signup/session + protected route in every template instead of letting the model invent it. • FOUNDATIONAL (quality) • Deps: T7 (backend), T33 for full-stack • **M** (SPA-only variant is **S**).

**T9 — Object storage for generated apps** — S3-compatible store (MinIO/Supabase) with upload helper + signed URLs, tenant-isolated prefixes. • SCALING • Deps: T7; tenant isolation model • **M**.

**T10 — Live preview + hot reload wiring** — Run the framework dev server inside the sandbox, expose via `<id>.preview.kodely` proxy subdomain, stream writes to disk so HMR pushes to the iframe. • FOUNDATIONAL (UX core) • Deps: **hard dep on sandbox (T3/T4)** + wildcard TLS + proxy router (related to T41) • **L** • Note: fundamentally different from today's build-then-serve model; this is a real architecture change.

**T11 — One-click deploy: Nxeon first, then Vercel/Netlify/CF** — Deploy button ships to Nxeon hosting (turning builders into hosting customers), with portability escapes. • FOUNDATIONAL (this is the monetisation moat) • Deps: **hosting infra**; T19 go-live flow; T30 partner API • **L**.

**T12 — Bi-directional GitHub sync** — Push generated code and pull external commits back so the AI works on true current state; GitHub App with per-repo tokens. • SCALING (retention of devs) • Deps: checkpoint/file-tree store (exists); conflict handling vs snapshots • **L**.

**T13 — Custom domains + automated SSL** — Attach user domains to deployed builds via existing Nxeon DNS/TLS automation. • SCALING • Deps: **hosting infra (T11)**, T41 router • **M** (reuses Nxeon pipeline).

**T14 — Project persistence: snapshot the filesystem, not just chat** — Git repo + periodic tarball snapshot + DB schema so a project rehydrates into a fresh sandbox. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: object storage; sandbox for rehydration • **M** • **LARGELY SATISFIED** — checkpoint snapshots of the full file tree already exist; remaining delta is git-as-source-of-truth and DB/migration capture.

**T15 — Multi-tenant isolation for sandboxes/previews** — Kernel/VM-level isolation, egress control, quotas, no shared creds; hard gate before real users. • FOUNDATIONAL (security gate) • Deps: **sandbox (T4)**, T32, T33 • **L** • Only becomes relevant once untrusted code *executes*; today's locked-tree `vite build` still runs untrusted code, so a scoped version is needed now.

**T16 — Secrets: encrypted vault + runtime injection, never in prompts** — Per-project vault, env injection into sandbox, output guardrail scanning commits for real secrets. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: sandbox for injection • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — publish-time secret scanning exists; the vault + runtime injection half does not.

**T17 — Per-branch preview envs with DB branching** — Throwaway preview URL + branched Postgres per AI iteration/branch. • OPTIMISATION (polish) • Deps: **T10 preview infra + T33 per-project DB** — near the top of the dependency chain • **L**.

**T18 — Sandbox cost control: hibernate, scale-to-zero, quotas** — Auto-hibernate idle projects, fast rehydrate from snapshot, per-plan CPU/RAM/runtime caps. • SCALING • Deps: **sandbox (T4)** + T14 snapshots • **M** • Mostly N/A until long-lived sandboxes exist; today's ephemeral build model has no idle burn.

**T19 — Go-live flow across Kodely↔Nxeon** — CTA → SSO account-link → signed partner API deploy + hosting subscription + coupon + card capture → `deploy.succeeded` webhook returns live URL. • FOUNDATIONAL (revenue path) • Deps: **hosting infra**, T30 contract, T26 webhooks • **L**.

**T20 — Cinematic scroll hero: how the effect works** — Explainer: scroll-scrubbed pre-rendered clip vs real 3D; division of labour between video model, scroll lib, and codegen. • OPTIMISATION (marketing/template) • Deps: none • **S** (it's a note) • Feeds T21/T22/T23.

**T21 — Zero-API procedural WebGL hero ($0 marginal)** — R3F + GSAP/Lenis + Bloom hero rendered live in the visitor's browser; default cinematic path, zero COGS. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: none • **M**.

**T22 — Seedance hero: prompt + scroll-scrub code (premium)** — Credit-gated bespoke path: AI-generated clip → ffmpeg image sequence → GSAP scrub. • OPTIMISATION (upsell) • Deps: credit system (A12); asset hosting • **M**.

**T23 — Working procedural WebGL hero demo (reference)** — A built proof of T21 exists at `scratchpad/kodely-webgl-hero.html`. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: none • **S** (done; needs productising) • **ALREADY BUILT** as a demo artifact.

**T24 — Recommended whole-system stack** — Master architecture card: Next.js/TS/Prisma/Postgres app, BullMQ+Redis worker queue, Claude router + caching, in-browser preview first then Firecracker, two output templates, Nxeon hosting. • FOUNDATIONAL (the spine) • Deps: names nearly every other card; **explicitly recommends deferring Firecracker until full-stack demand justifies it** • **XL** as a programme • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — model router + prompt caching + the agent loop already exist; the **build worker/queue (BullMQ+Redis)** is called out here and is a prerequisite for T28, T37, T18.

**T25 — Core data model / schema** — User, Org, Project, Build, Deployment, Domain, CreditLedger, Subscription, Template, Event, ApiToken. • FOUNDATIONAL — **do first; nearly everything reads/writes it** • Deps: none • **M**.

**T26 — Public API + webhooks** — REST API + project/deploy events; backs API tokens and the Nxeon go-live bridge. • SCALING • Deps: T25, T30 • **L**.

**T27 — Kodely CLI (init/deploy/pull)** — Power-user CLI reinforcing own-your-code positioning. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: T26 public API • **M**.

**T28 — Rate limiting, quotas, queue autoscaling** — Per-plan limits, build quotas, autoscale the build-worker pool. • SCALING • Deps: **build worker/queue (T24)**; T25 • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — coarse per-user rate limits exist; quotas + autoscaling do not.

**T29 — Disaster recovery + off-site backups (epic)** — Off-site backups, per-project DB+FS snapshot/restore, RTO/RPO, restore drills. Called the biggest infra gap. • FOUNDATIONAL (gate for hosting others' prod) • Deps: **hosting infra + per-project DB (T33)**; T14 • **L**.

**T30 — Kodely↔Nxeon partner API contract (formal spec)** — Signing, versioning, idempotency, auth, error semantics, webhook retry/DLQ. • FOUNDATIONAL — the monetisation moat rides on it • Deps: none to spec; blocks T19/T26 • **M**.

**T31 — CI/CD + staging + build isolation for Kodely itself** — Promote pipeline, migration gating, never build in the prod tree. • FOUNDATIONAL (Phase 0) • Deps: T39/T40 infra • **M**.

**T32 — Sandbox egress / SSRF firewall** — Allowlist blocking generated code from reaching internal metadata/DB/control plane. Hard pre-GA gate. • FOUNDATIONAL (security) • Deps: **sandbox (T4)** + T39 network topology • **M**.

**T33 — DB-per-project lifecycle + isolation** — Provisioning, isolated credentials, teardown, quota, backup per generated app. Security boundary, not a feature. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: T7 backend choice; **blocks T6, T8 full-stack, T17, T29** • **L**.

**T34 — Sandbox base-image supply chain + CVE patching** — Golden image with provenance and scheduled rebuilds. • SCALING • Deps: **sandbox (T4)** • **M** • Note: your existing single locked dependency tree is exactly this problem in miniature and already needs a patch cadence.

**T35 — Distributed tracing / request correlation** — End-to-end traces across app → queue → sandbox → partner API. • SCALING • Deps: **queue + sandbox** exist first • **M**.

**T36 — Data residency / region strategy** — EU pinning for generated apps + user data. • SCALING • Deps: **hosting infra**, multi-region sandbox pool • **L**.

**T37 — Load/chaos/capacity test of build-worker pool** — Validate autoscaling and rate limits under spike/failure before GA. • SCALING • Deps: **build worker/queue (T24) + T28** • **M**.

**T38 — Anthropic capacity: multi-key pool, org quota, spend caps** — Prevent a spike exhausting the key or the budget. • FOUNDATIONAL (launch blocker) • Deps: plugs into the existing model router • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — model router exists as the insertion point; key pool + hard spend caps do not.

**T39 — Kodely infra home: dedicated VMs isolated from Nxeon** — `kodely-app` VM (Next.js + worker + own Postgres) and a **separate** `kodely-sandbox` VM with nested KVM + Firecracker + hard egress firewall; capacity noted as sufficient to start. • FOUNDATIONAL — **the physical prerequisite for T4, T15, T32, T40** • Deps: Proxmox host • **L**.

**T40 — Staging environment (staging.kodely.me)** — prod + staging trees, staging Postgres, sandbox-staging target, CI promote with migration gating. Phase-0. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: T39 • **M**.

**T41 — *.kodely.site wildcard routing + subdomain router** — Separate PSL-listed domain, wildcard DNS + Cloudflare Universal SSL, plus a **new reverse-proxy component** mapping Host header → deployment; slug assignment, collisions, reserved names, takedown. • FOUNDATIONAL for free user hosting • Deps: **hosting infra + deployments must exist**; Phase 2 dispatch needs the sandbox • **L** (placeholder wildcard proving DNS/SSL is **S**).

**T42 — Credit burn is the #1 complaint; win on transparency** — Live credit meter, pre-flight cost estimate, never charge for a failed build. • FOUNDATIONAL (positioning wedge) • Deps: token metering (A12); **"never charge for a failed build" needs the existing self-repair loop's build-result signal** • **M**.

---

## AI / CODEGEN ENGINE (21)

**A1 — Flow-engineered agent loop (plan→generate→run→read errors→fix)** — Explicit state machine rather than one-shot generation; called the single most important engine decision. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: error capture (A4) • **L** • **SUBSTANTIALLY SATISFIED** — the self-repair loop (one retry with error fed back) is this loop in minimal form. Delta: multi-step planning, n>1 iterations, fix/ignore user choice.

**A2 — Diff-based edits over full-file rewrites** — Targeted patches for token cost + latency; full writes only for new files/large refactors. • OPTIMISATION (large, though) • Deps: none; pairs with A8 tools • **M**.

**A3 — Sonnet default, escalate to Opus for planning** — Model tiering behind a router. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: none • **S** • **ALREADY SATISFIED** — model router with configurable model + effort per build phase exists. Card is now just tuning.

**A4 — Instrument the sandbox to feed real errors back** — Capture build output, dev-server logs, runtime exceptions, **browser console errors**, structured into the next turn. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: **sandbox for the runtime/console half**; build-output half needs nothing • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — build errors already feed the repair loop; runtime + browser-console capture requires a live dev server, i.e. T10/T4.

**A5 — Context management: retrieve, don't dump** — Send tree/manifest but only relevant file bodies; context-rot degrades accuracy well before window limits. • FOUNDATIONAL for project growth (SCALING in timing) • Deps: A9 index • **L**.

**A6 — Prompt caching — biggest cost lever** — Cacheable stable prefixes (system prompt, tool defs, static project context). • OPTIMISATION • Deps: none • **S** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — caching on the system prompt exists; tool definitions and project-context prefixes are the remaining ~2 breakpoints.

**A7 — Context compaction / conversation summarization** — Summarize resolved turns, trim stale tool output, keep a rolling project-state summary. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: A1 loop • **M**.

**A8 — Tool-use design: fs, terminal, npm, console tools** — Lean composable tool set (write_file, apply_diff, read_file, run_command, install_package, read_logs, restart_dev_server). • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: **`run_command`/`install_package`/`restart_dev_server` require the sandbox and directly conflict with the locked-dependency-tree model** — install_package cannot exist without abandoning "never npm install per generation" or adding a curated allowlist • **M**.

**A9 — Retrieval/index over the project (tree + embeddings)** — Live symbol map + embeddings on pgvector so the agent searches instead of reading whole files. • SCALING • Deps: Postgres+pgvector; feeds A5, A21 • **L**.

**A10 — System prompt design + structured artifact output format** — Strict parseable schema (plan block, then file-write/shell actions) so the runner never parses prose. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: none; **prerequisite for making A6 caching effective** • **M** • Partially exists implicitly in the current builder.

**A11 — Stream generation to the UI** — Stream tokens, show each file as it's written, show plan up front, allow early interrupt. • FOUNDATIONAL (UX) • Deps: A10 output format • **M**.

**A12 — Token metering + credit system** — Per-user token/compute metering, credit balance, cost-per-project tracking, tied to Nxeon billing. Business-survival item. • FOUNDATIONAL • Deps: T25 (CreditLedger); **blocks T42, T22, T17 gating** • **L**.

**A13 — Execution-based evals: pass@k + regression harness** — Representative prompt suite that generates, boots, and asserts the app builds and core flows work; run on every prompt/model change. • FOUNDATIONAL (quality gate for every other engine change) • Deps: **needs a sandbox to boot apps for the flow-assertion tier**; the build-only tier works today with `vite build` • **L**.

**A14 — Guardrails: prompt-injection, secrets, code-injection scanners** — Input sanitisation of untrusted content (repos, issues, pastes) + output scanning (SecretsScanner, CodeInjectionScanner) as a launch gate. • FOUNDATIONAL (security) • Deps: T12 GitHub sync makes the injection surface real • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — publish-time secret scanning exists; prompt-injection input guardrails and code-injection scanning do not.

**A15 — shadcn/ui component retrieval for consistent UI** — Curated component/block library + a retrieval tool so the model composes known components instead of inventing markup. • OPTIMISATION (quality + tokens) • Deps: T5 template; A9-style retrieval • **M** • Fits today's locked dependency tree cleanly — no new install path needed.

**A16 — Model routing + graceful degradation/fallback** — Task-based routing, secondary provider on outage/rate-limit, degraded-mode banner, capped backoff retries. • OPTIMISATION/resilience • Deps: pairs with T38 key pool • **M** • **PARTIALLY SATISFIED** — router exists; fallback provider, degradation banner, and retry caps do not.

**A17 — Optional multi-agent decomposition (planner/coder/reviewer)** — Flag-gated reviewer pass for complex/paid builds; multiplies token cost. • OPTIMISATION • Deps: **A13 evals must exist to justify it**; A1 loop • **L** • Explicitly "start single-agent" — defer.
